9.6.2. qnav.input.config_handler

9.6.2.1. config_handler.py

summary:

This class provides a wrapper for Python’s ConfigHandler class. This supplies additional functionality such as automatically reading from sub-configuration files and providing platform independent means for extracting configuration values in usable formats.

authors:

Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk

version:

1.0.0 - First implementation of class.

class qnav.input.config_handler.ConfigHandler(config_file: Path = PosixPath('default_settings.ini'))[source]

This class provides means for reading the user’s configuration preferences from a given configuration file. Once read, values can be extracted within various formats (strings, booleans, floats, arrays, etc..). This class is essentially a wrapper for Python’s ConfigHandler class, providing additional functionality such as the ability to split configuration across multiple files.

get_config_name() → str[source]

This simple function returns the name of the configuration file being used. This function will automatically remove the project database_dir from the returned name (if the selected config is located within the project database_dir).

Returns:

The short name of the selected configuration file that is being used.

Return type:

str

load_configuration()[source]

This function reads and records the content of the given configuration file (and expected sub-files). Expected sections/sensors are automatically searched and their sub-files are also included within the loading process. This function can be used to re-load/re-read the information from configuration files (if changes are made during runtime).

append_config(config_file: str, from_section: str, to_section: str, to_overwrite: bool = False)[source]

This function will read and record the values of an external configuration files (i.e. a sub-configuration) and merge the read information with the current ConfigHandler instance.

Parameters:

  • config_file (str) – The sub-configuration file to read.

  • from_section (str) – The section within the sub-configuration file to read and record.

  • to_section (str) – The section within the current instance to append the read information to (can be a new section).

  • to_overwrite (bool) – If set to true, previous existing values from the main configuration will be overwritten by those read from sub-configuration files (default=False).

expand_section(section: str, path_property: str, sub_file_section: str = None, to_overwrite: bool = False)[source]

Expand section by importing the referenced sub-configuration path. Imports additional properties into section, for a given section and property referencing the sub-configuration file.

Parameters:

  • section (str) – The section containing the property with the sub-configuration path.

  • path_property (str) – The property containing the sub- configuration path.

  • sub_file_section (str) – (Optional) The section to import from the sub-configuration file.

  • to_overwrite (bool) – Should this import overwrite existing settings?

  • from_variable (numpy.typing.ArrayLike) – The filepath variable names from the given section stating the external configuration files to read from.

get_all_values() → ndarray[source]

This function returns a matrix containing all the values read from the given configuration file(s). This function is namely for debugging purposes. Values are displayed as raw strings.

Returns:

An N-by-3 matrix of values containing the section, variable name and value for each option read.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

get_sections()[source]

This function returns a list of all the sections read from the given configuration file(s). This is useful for debugging and ensure required content is being correctly read.

Returns:

A list containing all section names.

Return type:

list

get_str(section: str, name: str, fallback: str = None) → str[source]

This function will return the string value for a parameter in the selected configuration file, identified by its section and name. If the value is missing, an optional default value can be used instead.

Parameters:

  • section (str) – The section of the configuration file.

  • name (str) – The name of the variable to read from the given section.

  • fallback (str) – (Optional) The default value to use if not found.

Returns:

Returns either the string found within the config file for the given section and name, or the default value if not found.

str

get_bool(section: str, name: str, fallback: bool = None) → bool[source]

This function will return the boolean value for a parameter in the selected configuration file, identified by its section and name. Acceptable True values are ‘yes’, ‘true’, ‘on’ and ‘1’. Acceptable False values are ‘no’, ‘false’, ‘off’ and ‘0’. If the value is missing, an optional default value can be used instead.

Parameters:

  • section (str) – The section of the configuration file.

  • name (str) – The name of the variable to read from the given section.

  • fallback (bool) – (Optional) The default value to use if not found.

Returns:

Returns either the boolean found within the config file for the given section and name, or the default value if not found.

Return type:

bool

get_value_filepath(section: str, name: str, fallback: str | Path = None, must_exist: bool = False) → Path[source]

This function will return a local filepath read for a parameter in the selected configuration file, identified by its section and name. This function will handle read paths in a platform independent manner, automatically deciding and converting when needed. This allows paths read from the configuration file to be written in either Linux/Unix or Windows/NT format without affecting behaviour on different platforms.

Parameters:

  • section (str) – The section of the configuration file.

  • name (str) – The name of the variable to read from the given section.

  • fallback (str) – (Optional) The default value to use if not found.

  • must_exist – (Optional) Should the path exist on the filesystem? If enabled an error will raise if the given path is not found on the system (default=True).

Returns:

A valid filepath for the current system to the given location/resources.

Return type:

Path

get_value_filepath_str(section: str, name: str, fallback: str = None)[source]

This function will return a local filepath read for a parameter in the selected configuration file, identified by its section and name. This function will handle read paths in a platform independent manner, automatically deciding and converting when needed. This allows paths read from the configuration file to be written in either Linux/Unix or Windows/NT format without affecting behaviour on different platforms.

Unlike ‘get_value_filepath’ this function does not enforce the existence of a requested file/database_dir.

Parameters:

  • section (str) – The section of the configuration file.

  • name (str) – The name of the variable to read from the given section.

  • fallback (str) – (Optional) The default value to use if not found.

Returns:

A filepath for the current system to the given location/ resources. This resource does not have to exist.

Return type:

Path

is_value_set(section: list, value: list) → bool[source]

Returns true if there is an entry for (all of) the given sections and values. This function works for both single values and lists of values. For multiple values, both lists must be of the same length.

Parameters:

  • section (list or str) – A single or list of sections names.

  • value – A single or list of value names.

Returns:

True if an entry could be found in the provided configuration for all the given section-list pairs. False if one or more entries could not be found.

Return type:

bool

overwrite_value(section: str, name: str, new_value)[source]

This simple function can be used to overwrite or insert any value extracted from the given configuration file. This is only to be used for automatically generated values and is not an alternative to fallbacks.

Parameters:

  • section (str) – The section name of the variable to override

  • name (str) – The name of the variable to read from the given section.

  • new_value (str, int, float) – The new value to use for the given section and name.

copy_file(dest: Path)[source]

Copies the configuration file to a destination. This method produces a copy of the configuration file at the requested destination.

Parameters:

dest (Path) – The location to write the file to.

write_file(dest: Path)[source]

Writes the configuration values to a file. This method writes the configuration values in their current state (including modifications) to a requested file. The produced file can then be re-used as a settings file to repeat experimentation.

Parameters:

dest (Path) – The location to write the file to.

exception qnav.input.config_handler.NavConfigWarning[source]

A custom warning type used to inform the user about invalid, unsuitable or missing values present in the configuration file. If these warnings generated can be safely ignored, this warning type can be suppressed to hide all configuration file warnings for the session. Suppressing this warning type will not affect the displaying of other warnings.

exception qnav.input.config_handler.NavConfigError(section_name: str, variable_name: str, error_type: str, error_desc: str)[source]

A custom exception type used for inform the user about erroneous values present in the provided configuration file that cannot be ignored. This includes syntax, value type and conflicting value errors. This exception type is primarily used for formatting the errors being displayed. This custom class also allows configuration based errors to be distinguished from serious errors such faults not detected until after delivery.
